summary.intent: Execute Session 4 (work package Q, `just verify-real`) from the launch plan: build a local-registry rehearsal harness for release recovery scenarios, then commit and push with an explicit refspec, verify via git ls-remote, and add no session trailers.
summary.outcome: Built a TLS-based local-registry harness (Verdaccio, pypiserver, JSON simple index) with 5 passing `just verify-real` tests for npm partial-publish adoption and PyPI delayed/never-visible index, conflicting tag, and missing-artifact cases. Committed signed with no trailer and pushed HEAD:refs/heads/worktree-wp-q-verify-real, but the transcript ends before the ls-remote output is seen, and Cargo is not rehearsed.

repo: Callisto never opens sockets itself; all registry traffic goes through child processes (npm, curl, twine, cargo) that inherit the environment, so CA variables (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE) can trust a self-signed loopback cert without production changes.
The https-only registry rule accepts https on loopback, so local TLS registries bind through the real production binding and the http rejection test stays intact.
Production observation of PyPI requires the PEP 691 JSON simple index, which pypiserver cannot serve; a small stdlib Python JSON index server was needed for the index side.
pypiserver redirects unknown packages to a fallback with 303; the TLS variant needs `disable_fallback=True`.

Source replacement in cargo config does not redirect `cargo publish`; callisto always publishes with `--registry crates-io`, so a local cargo registry cannot be rehearsed and the real crates.io was contacted during a spike.
Tool pins live in .github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml; provisioning now goes through a `verify-real-tools` just recipe into target/verify-real/ so pins stay in one place.
Shared registry helpers were moved from release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs into tests/common/local_registries.rs, which now also hosts the npm fixture builders.

code.finding: The http-rejected-even-on-loopback test and the https-loopback-accepted test define the boundary that the harness relies on.
`execute` injects fake cargo credentials; a real-registry variant must omit them and set CA/TWINE/CARGO_HOME variables instead.
PyPI observation shells out to curl, so CURL_CA_BUNDLE controls TLS trust.

friction: Network was unavailable in the sandbox for git fetch, so it had to be retried unsandboxed.
The pip venv step failed and was redone with uv venv; later `--seed` had to be added.
pypiserver lacked JSON simple index support, forcing a custom index server.
Cargo spike hit real crates.io with a fake token before discovering publish ignores source replacement.
The gates failed once because earlier greedy replacements broke the old e2e test file's compile.
Delayed-visibility test had timing and partial-copy races, fixed with atomic rename, a 500ms poll, and distinct ports.
open_items: Cargo recovery scenario is not rehearsed because callisto hard-codes `--registry crates-io`; the dead cargo test code was dropped.
